(i) the most important factor determining the speed of convergence is the speed of diffusion of knowledge from the frontier to other economies, (ii) a high rate of diffusion of knowledge is associated with a high rate of human capital accumulation and a low rate of technological bias, (iii) a low rate of diffusion of frontier technologies is associated with a low rate of human capital and a high rate of technological bias.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the appropriate technology frontier for developing countries is not the technology frontier of developed countries, and it is not the technology of the past, but a technology that is appropriate for their own development.

the appropriate technology frontier for a country is the one that is most likely to promote the growth in the stock of human capital, and the most appropriate technology is that which is most likely to diffuse knowledge from abroad.
the appropriate technology for developing countries is the technology of the most developed countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a developing country should not be afraid of adopting the most appropriate technology available, regardless of whether this is the most advanced technology or the most skill-intensive technology.
a country's ability to grow depends crucially on its ability to acquire the appropriate technologies for its stage of economic development.
the developing world can learn from the developed countries.
